w: Darwin was bombed 64 times during the Second World War, and this museum sits right among the concrete gun emplacements built to stop it. The first raid, 19 February 1942, killed an estimated 243 people - other counts run far higher. Wartime hardware, still in position.
s: Where Darwin's WWII fortifications still stand guard.
_facts: Originally established as an artillery museum by the Royal Australian Artillery Association (NT)
Set amongst concrete gun emplacements and fortifications, one of Australia's most heavily fortified WWII sites
At the 1943 peak over 110,000 Allied armed forces personnel were based in and around Darwin
Darwin was bombed 64 times over almost two years during WWII
The first raid, 19 February 1942, is estimated to have killed 243 people, though other sources put the toll far higher; a memorial plaque on the Esplanade cites 292

w: Behind an unassuming name in the suburb of Winnellie sits a hangar of aircraft and engines tracing Northern Territory aviation history - once known as the Australian Aviation Heritage Centre, now a quieter monument to flight in the tropics.
s: Aircraft and engines telling the NT's aviation story.
_facts: Previously known as the Australian Aviation Heritage Centre
Displays aircraft and aircraft engines relevant to the Northern Territory and Australian aviation generally
Located in the Darwin suburb of Winnellie
